Full blizzard: thousands of individual white specks crowd the water so thickly the far rooftops dissolve into pale grey, each flake a separate soft point catching the warm amber light from the left side while the right sinks into deep blue shadow.

Last few flakes after the storm: seven or eight large lazy specks drift alone through water that is nearly clear, each one a distinct rounded flake tumbling end-over-end in slow motion, amber window-light from the little house below throwing a warm halo up around each passing one.

Snow rising: hundreds of fine white specks are moving upward off the rooftop ridges, each a tiny bright point lit from below by cold blue light bouncing off the settled white drifts, the dark water above them still and waiting to receive them back.

One enormous slow flake close to the glass, soft and faintly translucent, drifting down a full hand's-width ahead of a loose haze of much smaller specks far behind it, the near flake lit vivid warm gold while the distant haze stays cool and blue.

One whole side of the water is packed with hundreds of dense white specks crowding together, each still individually visible as a separate soft point, while the far side of the water holds only clear deep indigo, the boundary between them ragged and shifting.

Warm grey ash instead of snow: hundreds of soft irregular specks in pale charcoal and warm taupe drift slowly downward, each one catching a dim orange glow from a lit window below, settling into a fine grey ridge along the ridgeline of every roof.

Drifting pollen and dandelion seed: each suspended particle a tiny gold filament, dozens of them hanging nearly still at different depths in the water, the light coming in warm and amber from one side and igniting each filament into a thread of bright yellow against the deep green water behind.

Cherry petals turning as they fall: each a broad flat blush-pink petal rotating slowly on its own axis as it descends, the water catching them spread wide and face-on so the warm rose colour shows fully, lit from above in cold white that makes the pink saturate to almost red at the edges.

Fine silt and rising bubbles through a reef: hundreds of pale cream silt specks drifting upward alongside dozens of small distinct spherical bubbles, each bubble carrying a bright white highlight on its upper-left face and a shadow of deep teal beneath, the water itself thick and slow around them.

Grey moon dust hanging in perfectly still water: hundreds of fine pale silver-grey specks suspended absolutely still at every depth, each one holding its exact place, the cold blue light from directly above pressing down onto each speck and leaving the water between them an even, undisturbed deep navy.

Rain: thousands of short bright streaks, each one a distinct straight line of refracting white light about three millimetres long, all of them slanting left at the same angle through deep blue-grey water, the low amber light catching the top end of each streak and leaving the bottom end dark.

Golden sparks lifting off a bonfire: dozens of individual bright amber specks rising in a loose upward scatter, each one a separate warm orange point, the lowest ones lit most intensely in deep gold while the higher ones cool toward pale yellow against the dark brown water above the fire's glow.

Bright green flecks of aurora light suspended in the water itself: each a small rounded point of clear vivid green at a different depth and position, none of them moving, the cold deep blue of the surrounding water making each green point read as something close to electric, the whole field of them spread unevenly across the upper half.

Thirty or forty distinct spherical bubbles rising one behind another, each with a sharp white highlight and a deep teal shadow, all of them rising but angled fifteen degrees off vertical as though the world beneath them leans, the warm amber light from the lower left catching each sphere on its belly.

Sand drifting warm and brown over a caravan route: hundreds of individual specks in burnt sienna and pale ochre rolling slowly forward along the bottom of the water, each speck distinct and tumbling, the low warm orange light from the right side casting a long shadow behind every grain across the pale sandy bed below.

Confetti over a carnival: dozens of small flat specks in saturated cobalt, deep red, and bright yellow, each one a separate bright round scrap catching the warm white light from above on its flat face and flashing a different vivid colour as it rotates slowly downward through clear water.

Fireflies instead of flakes: forty or fifty individual warm amber pinpoints distributed through the dark water at irregular depths, none of them touching, each a distinct physical speck with a brighter core and a slightly softer edge, the surrounding water deep enough in blue-black to make each point read as its own small source of warmth.

Soap-bubble iridescence in the water where the light hits the surface tension low down: a dozen thin-walled spheres of different sizes drifting upward, each one showing a distinct band of deep violet along one edge and pale green along the opposite edge, the bands shifting position as each bubble rotates slowly in the warm side-light.

Snow with a fresh spin to it, the whole field of individual white specks moving in a wide slow arc as though the world was set down only a moment ago and the water still remembers the rotation, each speck a distinct soft point, the warm gold light catching the outermost ring of the spiral more brightly than the dark centre.

The tail end of a blizzard thinning out: the lower third of the water still holds hundreds of crowded white specks, each one distinct, but above them the specks grow fewer and more spread until the top of the water holds only cold blue depth and a dozen slow isolated flakes making their way down alone.

Snow packed against one side by a heavy invisible wind, each of the hundreds of individual white specks pressed close to the right edge of the water and moving rightward together at a low slant, the left side of the water deep and open in cool indigo, the warm amber light catching every speck on its left face as it travels.

Fine mist of ice crystals so small each one is only a single point of white, tens of thousands of them distributed through the full depth of the water, the cold blue light from above catching them across the whole upper half while the lower half glows faint amber from the lit windows of the world beneath, the surface of that world wavering slightly through the dense suspension.

Autumn leaves scaled down to specks: each a separate flat oval in deep ochre or burnt orange rotating slowly as it sinks, the warm side-light catching the upper face of each leaf-speck and leaving the underside in shadow so every one reads as a distinct three-dimensional object falling through the slow thick water.

A drift of tiny white specks collecting in a soft uneven ridge along the rooftop peak below, while above them the rest of the individual specks are still in motion, the settled layer at the bottom lit by cold blue from above pressing the white into bright relief against the dark wet surface of the roof beneath.

Bioluminescent plankton scaled to specks: hundreds of individual points in cold vivid cyan scattered through deep water the colour of midnight blue, each point a separate physical speck with a distinct bright face and a dark edge, the warm amber light from the lower left keeping strictly to its own side while the cold cyan holds the rest, each colour staying purely itself in the same water.
